newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
FINANCIAL TIMES
-- FORMER BARINGS MANAGER IN 0.5M STERLING CLAIM

A former senior manager at Barings Bank who was one of the people in charge of rogue trader Nick Leeson is to pursue her claim for a 500,000 sterling bonus which was promised to her hours before the discovery of the 830m sterling losses chalked up by Leeson. Mary Walz, former Barings global head of equity derivatives trading, was later sacked for her part in the collapse of the bank.
-- EU DELAYS END OF EXCLUSIVE AGREEMENTS

The European Union has decided to extend by two years regulations which allow some "exclusive agreements" in business to be exempt from anti-competition scrutiny. Areas affected by the exemptions include retailers and distributors of petrol, beer, luxury goods and perfumes. The issue is due to be looked at by the EU, but differences within the Commission on how to formulate new competition policy have forced the delay.
-- OIL COSTS PUT INFLATIONARY PRESSURE ON FACTORY PRICES

Figures released Monday show that higher oil prices impacted on British industry in September, forcing up manufacturer's fuel and raw material costs and prompting the first rise in factory output price inflation for 14 months. The retailer organization British Retail Consortium, is expected Tuesday to issue figures showing a strong rise in high street sales in September. However, fears of inflationary pressure will be countered by comments from BRC spokesman Andrew Higginson that prices are being held back by canny consumers.
-- UK CALL TO SCRAP EU ALUMINUM TARIFF

British aluminum producers, keen to see cheaper imports, have called for an end to the 6 percent tariff charged on about 60 percent of the aluminum imported by European Union countries. The move puts the UK industry at odds with its EU counterparts, with the British producers claiming that the tariff makes it more difficult for them to compete on a global market.
-- OFWAT GETS TOUGH WITH EARLY PRICE REVIEW

Water industry regulator Ofwat is set to announce a price review of water companies five years ahead of schedule. The move follows complaints that Ofwat director general Ian Byatt has been too lenient with the industry, which has been the subject of criticism over corporate greed. The last price review, conducted just two years ago, set price caps for the following ten years. The announcement of a mid-term review, planned for 1999, will come as a surprise to the industry.
-- OFGAS WARNS TRANSCO PROBE MAY WIDEN

Gas industry regulator Ofgas has referred its dispute with British Gas over price controls to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. However, regulator Clare Spottiswoode also said that Ofgas has left open the option of widening the terms of referral to include an investigation of the corporate structure of British Gas. The news has been seen as a veiled threat by British Gas, which is concerned that Ofgas may pursue previous threats to seek a separation of the pipeline business TransCo from the main British Gas business.
-- FRENCH GROUP OFFERS BLENHEIM STAKE

French water utility Compagnie Generale des Eaux has offered the British-based media group United News & Media the opportunity of acquiring its 15 percent stake in the exhibitions organiser Blenheim. United has been linked to Blenheim since the summer, but declined to comment on news of the CGE offer made on Monday. Dutch publishing and information services group VNU has already taken a 14.99 percent stake in Blenheim, and is expected shortly to move for another 10 percent, paving the way for a takeover battle with United if the British firm takes up the French offer.
-- PREMIER DISAPPOINTS ON INTERIMS

Premier Farnell, the world's third-largest electronic component distributor formed by the merger of Britain's Farnell Electronics with Premier Industrial Corporation of the US, has disappointed investors with the publication of its interim results. Pre-tax profits for the six months to July 28 were 56.1m sterling, following a 7.7m sterling exceptional charge for restructuring. The results were in line with expectations, but demonstrated little obvious benefit of the merger.
-- PHILIPS WARNS OF STAGNANT PROFITS

Philips, the Dutch consumer electronics group, has issued a warning of stagnant half-year profits, partly due to severe price competition across a range of the group's activities, the worldwide downturn in semiconductor demand, and the start-up costs of its latest venture, the digital phones market. Philips is expected to announce an internal shake-out when the company reports its third quarter results next week.
-- CHRYSLER BEATS EXPECTATIONS IN THIRD QUARTER

US car giant Chrysler has reported third-quarter results which show unexpectedly strong sales over the summer and put the company on track to equal its record annual after-tax earnings of $3.5 billion (2.3 billion sterling) reported in 1994. Announcing the results, the company also predicted that demand for new vehicles in the US was likely to remain strong for at least the rest of this year.
